correctness_confidence.basis: The 18-theorem Lean 4 kernel is verified with zero axioms (5 theorems) or standard foundations (13 theorems), 0 sorry, 0 warnings, and 0 Classical.choice. All algebraic identities, variance-hull bounds, SOS potentials, and Taylor approximations are mathematically sound.

novelty.basis: First machine-checked zero-floating-point formalization and exact-Q certificate auditor for the dynamic-stream Euclidean diameter algorithm of Giliberti & Hajiaghayi (2026), including dynamic ball-chain replay and red-team forgery rejection.

reproducibility.basis: Complete specification of 16 canonical certificates and 62 red-team adversarial test cases across four verification modes, with explicit runtime and bit-length analyses.

rigor.basis: Exhaustive verification across parallel-axis identities, Cauchy-Schwarz hull bounds, SOS margin bounds, two-cap spherical caps, and exact Taylor polynomial approximations without floating-point approximations.

significance.basis: Provides definitive computational and formal certification of recent breakthrough algorithms breaking the N^{2/3} update-time barrier in dynamic streams, establishing rigorous standards for streaming geometry.

potential_errors: Minor typographic alignment in Table 1 axiom footprints regarding zero-axiom vs propext/Quot.sound distinctions.
strengths: Zero-dependency Lean 4 18-theorem kernel with 0 sorry and 0 warnings.
Pure-stdlib exact-Q auditor (EUCLIDEAN-DIAM-CERT-1.0) auditing four distinct operational modes.
Comprehensive red-team adversarial evaluation rejecting 62/62 forgeries.
strong_novelty_candidates: Machine-checked exact-rational verification of dynamic-stream Euclidean diameter upper bounds and two-cap masks.
summary: The manuscript presents a rigorous machine-checked formalization and exact-rational certificate auditor (EUCLIDEAN-DIAM-CERT-1.0 alongside an 18-theorem Lean 4 kernel) for Giliberti and Hajiaghayi's dynamic-stream Euclidean diameter algorithm. The work achieves flawless zero-float verification across 16 canonical certificates and successfully rejects 62 live adversarial forgeries.
weaknesses: Scope is appropriately restricted to algebraic/geometric cores, leaving probabilistic Gaussian-grid couplings and space lower bounds as open targets.
